text:
Last spring the Avalanche beat the Wild in five games in the second round. The rematch arrives with both teams missing their best player. Nathan MacKinnon is out about 12 weeks with a lower-body injury, with ESPN estimating a mid-February return, and Quinn Hughes is out for Minnesota with an upper-body injury, listed as doubtful by The Hockey News and CBS Sports.

Colorado's answer so far has been Brock Nelson. He has stepped into MacKinnon's spot between Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen and is up to 19:40 a night, and Cale Makar came back from his own absence with three assists. The Avalanche have won three of four since, most recently a 6-0 win over Montreal in which Mackenzie Blackwood stopped all 28 shots. Blackwood is at .950 over his last five starts.

Minnesota has been the best story in the West. The Wild have 41 points in 27 games, a 99% chance at the playoffs by our numbers, and Kirill Kaprizov has 23 points in his last ten. Both his 15-game point streak and the team's ended on Wednesday in a 4-3 loss to Utah. A word of caution: their results are running ahead of their chances, a +37 goal difference on +20.8 expected, and Jesper Wallstedt's 16.19 goals saved above expected is doing a lot of that lifting. Without Hughes, Brock Faber has moved in beside Jonas Brodin and is playing 27:29 a night. Nick Foligno plays his 1,300th game.

Our numbers expect 3.05 goals for Minnesota and 2.86 for Colorado, close for two teams this good. Kaprizov sits at 46% to score and Matt Boldy at 42%. Devon Toews is the quiet one to watch for Colorado, with 10 points in his last 10 games.
headline: A playoff rematch with two stars missing
